name: PBB Games
shortDescription: Optional local games and preparedness-learning activities with safeguards for active incidents and emergencies.
longDescription: PBB Games / Tabulus is a lightweight optional engagement service made from local PHP and static assets. It offers locally installed games and preparedness-learning activities without a database or confirmed operational API dependencies.

Tabulus stays subordinate to emergency work. Active-incident mode hides recreational categories while emergency mode disables all games and directs users toward emergency guidance. The current control is configuration-driven and needs an operator runbook.

readiness.note: The local registry, mode policy, health endpoint, static assets, and emergency-mode safeguards are implemented without operational data dependencies.
remainingWork: Publish an operator runbook for changing mode during incidents.
Confirm whether future mode control remains manual or receives a reviewed local signal.
Review licensing and provenance before adding any third-party game assets.

problemSolved: A resilient local network should offer useful everyday engagement as well as emergency services, while ensuring recreational use never competes with active response priorities.

workflowSteps.title: Open the local activity hub
workflowSteps.description: A community member reaches Tabulus through the local PBB network after the optional package is installed.

workflowSteps.title: Choose an available activity
workflowSteps.description: The local registry displays only the games or preparedness activities permitted by the current mode.

workflowSteps.title: Protect emergency capacity
workflowSteps.description: Active-incident mode limits recreation, while emergency mode disables games and presents emergency guidance.

localCapabilities: Installed game and learning assets run locally without a database or public internet connection.
The mode policy and health summary are read from local configuration and registry files.
requiresLocalServices: Tabulus requires a local PHP/static host and its installed assets.
It uses vendored Helper UI assets but does not require operational PBB APIs in the confirmed V1.
syncsWhenConnected: No operational synchronization is required or confirmed for current game use.
Future package updates would be installation activity rather than live application data sync.
connectivityRequired: Users must be able to reach the local Games host over the node LAN.
The configured Hotline link must be reachable for emergency guidance navigation.
notSynchronized: No Hotline, Relay, Support, Realtime, Hub, Maestro, MapServer, or Kit Setup API calls are confirmed in V1.
Tabulus does not store or synchronize scores as operational PBB records in the reviewed implementation.

faqs.question: Why are games part of a resilience platform?
faqs.answer: Useful everyday activities give people a reason to know and use the local network before an emergency. Approved preparedness games can also support community learning.

faqs.question: What happens during an emergency?
faqs.answer: Emergency mode turns off all games and shows emergency guidance. During an active incident, recreational games are hidden, while approved learning activities may remain available.

faqs.question: Do installed games need internet access?
faqs.answer: No. Once installed, the current games and their files are stored on the local node and do not depend on a cloud service.

faqs.question: Does Tabulus call Hotline or Relay APIs?
faqs.answer: No. The reviewed V1 does not show Tabulus exchanging operational information with Hotline, Relay, or the other PBB services.

faqs.question: Does Tabulus keep a community member database?
faqs.answer: No. The reviewed version does not use a community member database. It works as a simple local game catalog with settings for operating modes.

faqs.question: Who changes the emergency mode?
faqs.answer: The mode is currently changed through system settings. The exact person or automatic process responsible for changing it still needs to be documented and approved.
